text:
Predicates:
Allowed(x) ::: Pets are allowed in building x.
DepositRequired(x) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in building x.
EqualDeposit(x) ::: The security deposit in building x is equal to one month's rent.
MoreDeposit(x) ::: The security deposit in building x is more than one month's rent.
Owns(tom, fluffy) ::: Tom owns a pet cat named Fluffy.
Pet(x) ::: x is a pet.
Building(x) ::: x is a building.
RentAmount(x, y) ::: The monthly rent at building x is $y.
MoveInWith(tom, fluffy) ::: Tom is allowed to move in with Fluffy.
Premises:
∃x (Building(x) ∧ Allowed(x)) ::: Pets are allowed in some managed buildings.
∀x (Building(x) → DepositRequired(x)) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building.
∀x (DepositRequired(x) → (EqualDeposit(x) ∨ MoreDeposit(x))) ::: The security deposit can be either equal to one month's rent or more.
Owns(tom, fluffy) ∧ Pet(fluffy) ::: Fluffy is Tom's cat and cats are pets.
Building(oliveGarden) ∧ Allowed(oliveGarden) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building.
RentAmount(oliveGarden, 2000) ::: The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000.
MoveInWith(tom, fluffy) ↔ (DepositRequired(oliveGarden) ∧ ¬MoreDeposit(oliveGarden)) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if and only if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500.
2000 > 1500 ::: $2000 is more than $1500.
Conclusion:
MoveInWith(tom, oliveGarden) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in The Olive Garden.
